rationales: Sr-90 is not used for diagnosing thyroid goiter.
Co-60 is used mainly in radiotherapy, not thyroid diagnosis.
I-131 is taken up by the thyroid and is used to diagnose thyroid disorders such as goiter.
C-14 is used as a tracer in other applications, not for diagnosing goiter.
Fluorine has the highest electronegativity of these elements.
Chlorine is less electronegative than fluorine.
Bromine is less electronegative than chlorine and fluorine.
Iodine is less electronegative than the other listed halogens.
Non-metals typically form covalent bonds by sharing electrons.
Ionic bonds usually form between metals and non-metals through electron transfer.
A coordinate covalent bond is a special type of covalent bond and is not the general expected answer.
Metallic bonds form between metal atoms.
The electronegativity difference is approximately 1 using the values typically given in this course.
A difference of 2 is greater than the approximate difference between hydrogen and chlorine.
A difference of 3 is too large for hydrogen and chlorine.
A difference of 4 is not the electronegativity difference between hydrogen and chlorine.
Chlorine is a gas at room temperature.
Bromine is a liquid at room temperature.
Fluorine is a gas at room temperature.
Iodine is a solid at room temperature.
An aqueous acid solution conducts electricity because it contains ions.
A sugar solution does not produce ions and is a non-electrolyte.
A NaOH solution conducts electricity because it contains ions.
A Ca(OH)₂ solution conducts electricity through its dissolved ions.
Butter is a gel-type colloid with liquid dispersed in a solid or semi-solid medium.
Fog consists of liquid droplets dispersed in a gas.
Opal is a solid dispersed in a solid medium.
Sugar in water is a solid dissolved in a liquid, not a liquid in a solid.
Chlorine does not have one valence-shell electron.
Chlorine has more than six valence electrons.
Chlorine has seven electrons in its outer shell.
Eight is the full outer-shell count for chlorine’s next shell, not its valence-shell count.
An ionic bond forms through electron transfer, not donation of a shared pair.
In an ordinary covalent bond, each bonded atom contributes an electron to the shared pair.
A metallic bond involves delocalized electrons among metal atoms.
In a coordinate covalent bond, one bonded atom donates both electrons in the shared pair.
Atomic radius generally decreases from left to right across a period.
Ionization energy generally increases from left to right across a period.
Electron affinity generally becomes more favorable across a period, rather than decreasing as the usual trend.
Electronegativity generally increases from left to right across a period.
The L shell can hold more than six electrons.
The L shell holds a maximum of 2n² = 2(2)² = 8 electrons.
Fourteen exceeds the L shell’s capacity.
Eighteen exceeds the L shell’s capacity.
Benzene, C₆H₆, reduces to the empirical formula CH.
C₂H₂ reduces to CH, but is not the stated empirical formula.
HO is not the empirical formula of benzene.
CH₂O is not the empirical formula of benzene.
The valence electrons of group 1 and group 2 elements occupy s orbitals, so they are s-block elements.
The p block comprises elements whose last electrons enter p orbitals.
The d block comprises transition elements whose differentiating electrons enter d orbitals.
The f block comprises elements whose differentiating electrons enter f orbitals.
Liquids are typically much denser than gases by more than a factor of ten.
A factor of 100 is below the usual approximate comparison.
A liquid is approximately 1000 times denser than a gas in the textbook comparison.
A factor of 10000 is far above the usual approximate comparison.
Percent m/m is grams of solute per 100 grams of solution.
Percent m/v is grams of solute per 100 millilitres of solution.
Percent v/m is millilitres of solute per 100 grams of solution.
Percent v/v is millilitres of solute per 100 millilitres of solution.
